title: Fynaptix · Quantum Computing Research
heading: Quantum Computing Intelligence
subheading: Pure-plays, hedged giants & the road to commercial advantage
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Quantum pure-plays trade at extreme valuations (P/S ~64–514×) and are highly speculative — position sizing matters more here than anywhere else on this hub. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Every major name moved higher this week: IonQ rebounded 6.5% to $39.13 (Sep 17), Rigetti rose 5.4% to $16.10, D-Wave added 1.8% to $17.11, and Quantinuum led the group, up 10.7% to $54.50 (Sep 18) on its continuing error-correction and CHIPS momentum. The Defiance Quantum ETF (QTUM) was the outlier, slipping 3.2% to $142.74 on broader tech-sector rotation even as single names rallied

IBM's Anderon subsidiary finalized a $1B CHIPS and Science Act award (Sep 16) — the largest single quantum award to date — to scale its 300mm pure-play quantum wafer foundry in Albany, NY, with IBM matching another $1B in cash, IP, assets and workforce. That's on top of the $400M in $100M-each awards to D-Wave, Rigetti, Quantinuum and PsiQuantum finalized the prior week, bringing September's total federal quantum CHIPS commitment to roughly $1.4B

IonQ $39.13 (~$15.85B mkt cap / ~$246.5M TTM revenue, P/S ~64×) / Rigetti $16.10 (~$5.38B / ~$13.4M TTM, P/S ~401×) / D-Wave $17.11 (~$6.38B / ~$12.4M TTM, P/S ~514×); Quantinuum (QNT) $54.50 (Sep 18, ~$14.3B mkt cap) against just $28-32M in FY26 revenue guidance; Defiance Quantum ETF (QTUM) at $142.74 (Sep 15), still well below its 52-week high of $170

tiers.label: Hedged Giants — Quantum as an Option
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list. Most quantum systems remain in R&D; true commercial systems are likely years away.

rows.angle: The single biggest quantum-specific catalyst of the month: Anderon, IBM's quantum-foundry subsidiary, finalized a $1B CHIPS and Science Act award (Sep 16) — converting a May letter of intent into a definitive agreement — to expand its 300mm pure-play quantum wafer foundry in Albany, NY, matched by another $1B in IBM cash, IP, assets and workforce. First quantum wafers are already running through the facility, supporting superconducting qubit arrays and readout signal-chain components
rows.watch for: Yield and qualification ramp at the Albany 300mm line; Anderon's planned extension into other quantum modalities beyond superconducting; how this $2B combined commitment nets against IBM's broader $10B quantum commercialization pledge

rows.angle: Another comparatively quiet week for Willow-specific hardware milestones; the UK's National Quantum Computing Centre access program continues to move forward, with researchers now able to submit proposals to design and run experiments on Google's 105-qubit Willow chip in search of practical applications
rows.watch for: Concrete results from the first UK NQCC access-program experiments; any hardware advance beyond memory preservation; specifics on Google Quantum AI's reported neutral-atom exploration; any competitive response to IBM's Anderon foundry news or NVIDIA's CUDA-Q Logical launch

rows.angle: A quieter week directly for Microsoft, but its Quantinuum partnership kept compounding: Quantinuum shares rose another 10.7% to $54.50 (Sep 18) as the market continues digesting last week's Helix error-correction validation and CHIPS award, with Quantinuum set to appear at Quantum World Congress 2026 (Sep 23-25)
rows.watch for: Any fresh Quantinuum scaling results ahead of Quantum World Congress; commercial deals stemming from the Saudi Aramco MOU; Majorana milestone reproducibility on Microsoft's own topological-qubit program

rows.angle: NVIDIA's most active week in the sector in over a month: expanded the open-source CUDA-Q platform with a new "CUDA-Q Logical" orchestration layer for fault-tolerant computing (Sep 14) — Fermilab used it to cut fault-tolerant architecture development from five months to three weeks, a 7x speedup, and Sandia's QUOPS benchmark is now built in; separately, NVIDIA's NVQLink ran its first end-to-end program across live qubits, GPUs and CPUs with Quantum Machines (Sep 13), and NVentures (NVIDIA's venture arm) was reported participating in fresh funding alongside QuEra's neutral-atom program
rows.watch for: Adoption of CUDA-Q Logical by additional national labs and hardware partners; further NVQLink integrations beyond Quantum Machines; confirmation and terms of the QuEra investment

tiers.label: Pure-Plays — Highly Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list. Most quantum systems remain in R&D; true commercial systems are likely years away.

rows.angle: A strong bounce-back week on substance rather than guidance: IonQ and Synopsys demonstrated quantum-accelerated gains in large-scale computer-aided engineering workflows, cutting execution time up to 14.6% (Sep 17) and taking 1st place Best Paper at IEEE Quantum Week 2026 — one of four Best Paper awards IonQ collected there. Separately, an ORNL/IonQ/NVIDIA/UT Knoxville collaboration introduced DQAOA-GPT (Sep 16), a generative-AI framework that synthesizes quantum optimization circuits in a constant 28 seconds
rows.watch for: Stock recovered 6.5% to $39.13 (Sep 17) after the prior week's post-Investor-Day slide; consensus target still ~$69.25 (Strong Buy); P/S ~64×, still the cheapest of the pure-play trio; delivery progress on the Superion 256 platform ordered at Investor Day

rows.angle: DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative Stage B roster is now confirmed: eleven companies advanced (Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM, IonQ, Nord Quantique, Photonic, Quantinuum, Quantum Motion, QuEra, Silicon Quantum Computing, Xanadu) — Rigetti is not among them, formalizing the exclusion flagged in prior weeks. Q2 revenue of $5.1M (+185% YoY) and last week's $100M CHIPS award remain the more constructive data points
rows.watch for: Stock $16.10 (Sep 18, +5.4% on the week, mostly riding the broader sector rally rather than company-specific news); consensus target ~$28.81 (Buy); P/S ~401×; whether Rigetti can still enter QBI Stage B via separate negotiation, as DARPA has left open for some Stage A participants

rows.angle: A genuinely mixed week: real commercial validation, as D-Wave's technology now powers a second production application at NTT DOCOMO in Japan, cutting peak location-registration signals 65.3% and paging signals 7.0%, and BMO Capital initiated coverage at Outperform with a $35 target citing first-mover edge and its dual-technology (annealing plus gate-model) strategy. But Q2 revenue of $3.08M missed the $4.03-4.08M consensus by roughly 24-25%, triggering a fresh round of legal scrutiny on top of the securities-litigation investigation that already spans four law firms
rows.watch for: Stock $17.11 (Sep 18, +1.8% on the week); consensus target ~$35.24 (Strong Buy) despite the overhangs; P/S ~514×, still the richest multiple in the sector; D-Wave's dual-rail gate-model architecture update and platinum-sponsor showcase at Quantum World Congress 2026 (Sep 23-25)

rows.angle: French neutral-atom quantum computer builder chaired by Nobel laureate Alain Aspect; completed its SPAC merger with Bleichroeder Acquisition Corp. II and began trading on Nasdaq Aug 28 with ~$360M cash; customers include Saudi Aramco and LG Electronics
rows.watch for: Shares roughly flat at $7.94 (Sep 17) versus $7.92 the prior week, still well below the $19.11 debut-day close (Aug 28) and the original $9.79 SPAC reference price, on still no new company-specific news; first reporting quarter as a listed company still pending

private_watchlist.name: PsiQuantum
private_watchlist.note: Reportedly closed a $1.5B round (May 2026) at a ~$10.5B valuation; broke ground on its Moreton Bay Central fault-tolerant facility in Australia. A quieter week following last week's Brookhaven National Laboratory partnership and its own $100M CHIPS Act award: PsiQuantum presented tutorials, research talks and panels on fault-tolerant quantum computing and its Construct PsiQDK software platform at IEEE Quantum Week 2026 in Toronto, continuing to build the DARPA/AFRL/GlobalFoundries manufacturing ecosystem around its photonic approach.

private_watchlist.name: Quantinuum
private_watchlist.note: Honeywell-backed; upsized $1.68B IPO raise at $60/share. Shares extended last week's rally, rising another 10.7% to $54.50 ($12.9B → ~$14.3B mkt cap, Sep 18) as the market continues to reward its validated Helix error-correction architecture and $100M CHIPS Act award. Quantinuum is now a confirmed Stage B participant in DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative and is set to appear at Quantum World Congress 2026 (Sep 23-25). FY26 revenue guidance remains just $28-32M against that valuation — a widening gap even as the technical story strengthens.

private_watchlist.name: QuEra
private_watchlist.note: $230M+ raise backed by Google Quantum AI, SoftBank, NVentures; 96 verified logical qubits (Nature) — industry-leading; confirmed as one of eleven companies advancing to DARPA QBI Stage B. New this week: NVIDIA's venture arm (NVentures) was reported participating in fresh funding alongside QuEra as part of a broader NVIDIA push across multiple quantum hardware approaches. QuEra reiterated its roadmap toward a third-generation machine (~100 logical qubits, ~10,000 physical qubits) and a future system exceeding 20,000 physical qubits aimed at a billion logical operations.

bear_case.title: Years from commercial advantage
bear_case.description: Most systems remain R&D-phase; revenue today is mostly government contracts, research access and early pilot deployments rather than broad commercial workloads. D-Wave's own Q2 revenue of just $3.08M — a 24-25% miss versus consensus — is a reminder that even companies with real production wins (like the NTT DOCOMO deployment) are still working off a tiny base.

bear_case.title: A rally doesn't erase execution risk
bear_case.description: Every major pure-play and private-market name rose this week on a wave of CHIPS Act and NVIDIA-platform news, but D-Wave's stock still climbed despite a 24-25% revenue miss and widening securities-litigation scrutiny, and Rigetti's DARPA QBI exclusion was formally confirmed the same week its shares rose 5.4% on sector sentiment alone. Sector-wide enthusiasm can paper over company-specific problems for a while, not indefinitely.

bear_case.title: Insiders aren't buying — and the number keeps growing
bear_case.description: Insiders at IonQ, Rigetti and D-Wave have now sold a net of roughly $988M in stock over the trailing five years (up from the ~$863M/three-year figure cited a month ago), with virtually no offsetting insider buying even as fresh government CHIPS equity stakes pile a new class of shareholder on top of an already dilution-heavy funding model.

bear_case.title: Dilution as a business model
bear_case.description: Pure-plays continue to fund R&D via repeated equity raises and government equity stakes; share counts grow relentlessly. Quantinuum's post-IPO financials show an even wider gap between $28-32M FY26 guidance and its now ~$14.3B market cap after this week's 10.7% rally, and Pasqal remains stuck near $7.94 — still roughly 60% below its debut-day close three weeks in — a reminder that new entrants are still priced on story, not statements.

bear_case.title: Winner may not be listed — or may be a giant's subsidiary
bear_case.description: IBM's Anderon just landed the largest quantum CHIPS award to date ($1B, matched by another $1B from IBM) for a wafer foundry that is neither a pure-play stock nor a venture-backed startup — it's a wholly-owned IBM subsidiary. Combined with PsiQuantum's and QuEra's continued private-market progress, this week reinforced that a meaningful share of the technology roadmap sits outside anything an investor can buy directly as a pure-play.

catalysts.title: FIPS 140-2 sunset takes effect
catalysts.description: NIST's Cryptographic Module Validation Program moved all remaining FIPS 140-2 validated certificates to the Historical list; only FIPS 140-3 validated implementations are now accepted for new federal procurement, a concrete step in the post-quantum cryptography migration mandated by June's executive order.

catalysts.title: D-Wave's Q2 revenue miss draws fresh legal scrutiny
catalysts.description: Q2 revenue of $3.08M missed consensus of $4.03-4.08M by roughly 24-25%, adding to the securities-litigation investigation that already spans four law firms, even as BMO Capital initiated coverage at Outperform the same week.

catalysts.title: IonQ and Synopsys win Best Paper at IEEE Quantum Week
catalysts.description: Their joint demonstration of quantum-accelerated computer-aided engineering workflows cut execution time up to 14.6% and took 1st place Best Paper — one of four such awards IonQ collected at the conference.

catalysts.title: IBM's Anderon finalizes $1B CHIPS Act quantum foundry award
catalysts.description: The largest single quantum CHIPS award to date, funding expansion of Anderon's 300mm pure-play quantum wafer foundry in Albany, NY, matched by another $1B in IBM cash, IP, assets and workforce.

catalysts.title: NVIDIA launches CUDA-Q Logical for fault-tolerant computing
catalysts.description: The new orchestration layer let Fermilab cut fault-tolerant architecture development from five months to three weeks (a 7x speedup) and now incorporates Sandia's QUOPS benchmark for utility-scale readiness.

catalysts.title: NVIDIA NVQLink runs first end-to-end quantum-GPU program
catalysts.description: Quantum Machines used NVQLink to route quantum and classical tasks across live qubits, GPUs and CPUs in a single program, exchanging measurements and control decisions in microseconds — the real-time responsiveness needed for quantum error correction.

etfs.name: Defiance Quantum
etfs.summary: Quantum + advanced computing basket — at $142.74 (Sep 15, -3.2% on the week even as most single names rallied), well below its 52-week high of $170; ~$5.5B+ AUM; the standard diversified route

etfs.summary: Indirect: the compute substrate quantum must beat (and currently rides)

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: IBM
positions.note: The single biggest quantum catalyst of the month: Anderon finalized a $1B CHIPS Act award (Sep 16) for its Albany 300mm quantum wafer foundry, matched by another $1B from IBM itself. Nudged up on the scale and specificity of that commitment; still a rounding error on a profitable, dividend-paying business.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.note: A fifth straight quiet week for Willow-specific hardware milestones; the UK NQCC access program is progressing but has yet to produce a concrete result. Trimmed to fund this week's stronger NVIDIA and IonQ catalysts; also your largest AI-sleeve holding, so size this weight with that overlap in mind.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: No new Microsoft-specific catalyst this week, but its Quantinuum partnership keeps compounding as QNT shares rose another 10.7% to $54.50 on continuing Helix/CHIPS momentum. Held steady pending fresh news around Quantum World Congress (Sep 23-25); also held in the AI sleeve — avoid double-counting.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: NVIDIA's most active week in the sector in over a month: the new CUDA-Q Logical layer gave Fermilab a 7x development speedup, NVQLink ran its first live end-to-end quantum-GPU program with Quantum Machines (Sep 13), and NVentures reportedly joined QuEra's funding. Bumped up on the breadth of concrete, company-specific progress; also your largest cross-sector AI holding, so size for that concentration too.

positions.name: IonQ
positions.note: Recovered 6.5% to $39.13 on substance rather than guidance: a Best Paper win with Synopsys on quantum-accelerated CAE (14.6% faster execution) and the ORNL/NVIDIA DQAOA-GPT circuit-synthesis framework. Nudged up on the pivot from guidance-driven hype to peer-reviewed technical validation; still the cheapest pure-play on P/S (~64×).

positions.name: Rigetti
positions.note: DARPA formally confirmed Rigetti is not among the eleven companies in QBI Stage B, closing off a key optionality thesis flagged as pending in prior weeks. This week's 5.4% share gain rode broad sector sentiment, not company-specific news, so weight is trimmed toward the minimum while the CHIPS award and Purdue partnership keep this a Speculative rather than a Watch/Avoid.

positions.name: Quantinuum
positions.note: Shares are up 10.7% on top of last week's rally to a ~$14.3B market cap, while FY26 revenue guidance is unchanged at $28-32M — the valuation gap is widening faster than the (genuinely real) technical progress justifies. Trimmed toward the minimum: price has outrun fundamentals even though the underlying Helix/CHIPS story is intact. Also note the Aramco relationship overlaps with Microsoft's own AI-sleeve exposure.

positions.name: D-Wave
positions.note: A real commercial win — a second production deployment at NTT DOCOMO cutting signaling load double digits — and a fresh BMO Capital Outperform rating are genuine positives. But a Q2 revenue miss of 24-25% versus consensus, on top of the CFO transition and a securities-litigation investigation now spanning four law firms, means the open questions that justified Avoid last week are still open.

positions.name: Pasqal
positions.note: Essentially flat at $7.94 versus $7.92 last week, still nearly 60% below its Aug 28 debut-day close with zero new company-specific news and no independent public financials yet. Nothing this week changes the case against holding it.
